notes: Episodes: the first session the condition is on after 20 sessions without it. Outcomes: the forward 21/63/126-session return of the proxy and of the equal-weight universe index, and the worst further drop within 63 sessions.

Baselines: every session of the same period (unconditional; n_eff = n / horizon is the rough count of independent windows) and the naive rule 'proxy 10% or more under its 252-day high', de-clustered the same way.

verdict compares the episodes' mean with the baseline mean on the episodes' own standard error: 'above' or 'below' needs |z| >= 2; under 10 episodes it says 'too few to conclude'. Episodes 20 sessions apart still share most of a 63- or 126-session window, so even these z values overstate independence.
Look-ahead: flags use expanding percentiles and fixed thresholds only; the test suite proves a flag on a date does not change when later data is appended.

Survivorship: the universes are today's ticker list, so names that were delisted, acquired or dropped are missing and names were added partly because they did well. Past breadth therefore reads healthier than the real universe was, and the equal-weight index's forward returns are biased upward for episodes and baseline alike; the comparison with the baseline is less biased than either level.

History depth: prices.db starts 2016-08 for most long-lived names, the sector ETFs included (backfilled 2026-11-17); the test period begins once every rule has a year of its own observations (the relative-volume rule only counts down days, so about 2019), which leaves roughly seven years and a handful of real drawdowns (2020, 2022, 2025).

backtest.vix: the curve's two flags (the first session of each inversion episode; the un-inversion session) and 'universe capitulation K>=3 on a session the curve is inverted', each measured on SPY and SMH with the same de-clustering, horizons and verdicts. Each block has its own period and its own baselines (every session of that period; SPY's and SMH's own 10% drawdown rule). The flags need no warm-up, so their period starts with the VIX3M history (2016-08); the combination starts with the universe's test period.
backtest.read: In the two stock universes, 76 capitulation and turn-signal cells (rule x horizon x proxy or equal-weight index) had 10 or more independent episodes: 0 beat the any-day forward return by two standard errors, 0 trailed it and 76 showed no measurable difference (the average was higher in 42 of them, which is a lean, not evidence); 92 more cells had too few episodes to conclude anything. Against simply buying any 10% drawdown of the proxy there is no measurable edge: 46 testable cells, none better (46 no difference, 0 worse). The sector-ETF set (2019-02-26 to 2026-11-17): 42 cells testable, 0 above the any-day return, 0 below, 42 no measurable difference (42 too few); against buying a 10% drawdown, 0 better, 0 worse. The VIX curve (inversion, un-inversion, and capitulation K>=3 while inverted, on SPY and SMH): 30 cells testable, 0 above the any-day return, 0 below, 30 no measurable difference (0 too few); against buying a 10% drawdown, 0 better, 0 worse. No rule here shows a measurable edge; read today's counts as a description of how washed-out the tape is, not as a timing signal.

method: Settled daily closes only (adjusted close for returns and averages; the day's high, low and close as printed for the proxy's close location; dollar volume = close x volume). Intraday is out of scope.
Each member's averages, lows, relative volume and RSI are computed on its own bars; a session with no bar for a name is skipped for that name, never filled.

A universe's session is null when fewer than the minimum members have a bar (15 for the stock universes, 8 for the ETF set) or fewer than half of today's live members do, so the readings never silently change meaning as the list grows.

Percentiles are expanding-window: each session is ranked only against the same reading on that session and earlier ones (mid-rank for ties), oriented so a HIGH percentile always means MORE exhausted. None until a reading has 252 observations; pctile_obs and pctile_since give the window behind today's figure.
Extreme rules are fixed in advance in the thresholds block and were not tuned on the backtest.

capitulation_count is how many of the capitulation rules are on; capitulation_of is how many could be evaluated. turn_signals lists which of divergence, breadth thrust and follow-through day fired in the last 10 sessions. There is no blended score.

The ETF set is small: each member moves a share reading by about two points, and members overlap heavily. Its price history was backfilled to 2016-08 on 2026-11-17 (a few members launched later and join when they start trading).

The vix block is market-wide context and is NOT counted in any universe's capitulation_count. VIX, VIX9D and VIX3M are Cboe index closes; ratio_1m_3m = VIX / VIX3M, ratio_9d_1m = VIX9D / VIX. inverted = VIX / VIX3M above 1.0 (backwardation: near-term fear priced above three-month); uninverted_within_10 = inverted on one of the previous 10 sessions and not today. The block is absent when any of the three series is missing.

The latest session's volume is the figure the nightly fetch sees shortly after the close; the provider often revises it the next day, so today's relative-volume and follow-through readings can move on rerun.
Display only. Nothing here is a forecast or an instruction.

_turn.divergence: Equal-weight index at a 60-session closing low, an earlier 60-session low within 60 sessions separated by at least 5 sessions off the low, and the share at 20-day lows now below its reading on that earlier low.
_turn.ftd: 4 to 12 sessions after the proxy's most recent 60-session closing low, the proxy up 1.5% or more on volume above the prior session's.
_turn.thrust: 10-session EMA of advancers/(advancers+decliners) crosses above 0.615 having been below 0.40 within the previous 10 sessions (Zweig's levels).

_vix.inverted: VIX / VIX3M above 1.0: the curve in backwardation, 30-day fear priced above 3-month. The conventional line, fixed in advance.
_vix.pctile: Every continuous VIX reading carries an expanding percentile, high = more fear.
_vix.uninverted_within_10: Inverted on one of the previous 10 sessions and not today: the curve returning to contango, fixed in advance.

above_200d.label: Share above their 200-day average
above_200d.why: No level is standard for a list this size and this growth-heavy; its own 95th percentile.

above_20d.label: Share above their 20-day average
above_20d.why: Classic short-term oversold breadth level: 15% or fewer above the 20-day.

above_50d.label: Share above their 50-day average
above_50d.why: Classic intermediate washout level: 20% or fewer above the 50-day.

close_loc.label: Proxy close location in the day's range
close_loc.why: Proxy down 1% or more AND closing in the bottom tenth of its range: selling into the close.

dist_50d.label: Median distance from the 50-day average
dist_50d.why: How stretched below trend the typical name is; its own 95th percentile.

down90_10d.label: 90% down days in the last 10 sessions
down90_10d.why: Two or more 90% days close together is the classic capitulation cluster.

down_vol.label: Down-volume share (dollar volume)
down_vol.why: The 90% downside day (Lowry): nine-tenths of the money traded in names that fell.

low_20d.label: Share at a 20-day closing low
low_20d.why: 40% or more of members at a 20-day closing low is a broad liquidation day.

low_252d.label: Share at a 252-day closing low
low_252d.why: Yearly lows are rare and list-dependent; its own 95th percentile.

rsi14.label: Median 14-day RSI (Wilder)
rsi14.why: The conventional oversold line, applied to the median member.

vol_surge.label: Median relative volume on a down day
vol_surge.why: Volume against each name's own 50-day average, only on days the universe fell; its own 95th percentile.

coverage.label: Coverage single stocks
coverage.rule: Every US-listed single stock in tickers.txt: no ETFs, indices, futures, FX, crypto or foreign-exchange listings. Proxy SPY.

market.label: Sector and industry ETFs
market.rule: The rotation ladder's GICS sector and industry ETF rows, one per twin group, no baskets, no broad/region/theme rows, not SLV. A small N: each member moves a share reading by several points, and members overlap heavily.

semis.label: Semis and AI hardware
semis.rule: The single stocks technicals.py proxies to SMH, i.e. the sections: AI compute / datacenter operators; Memory & storage; Optics / networking; Semiconductors: compute, design, analog/power. Proxy SMH.
